tips.alwaysOn: Background load is what the home draws when nobody is using anything: router, chargers, devices on standby. Every 10 W running all year costs about 88 kWh.
tips.fridge: Keep it 10 cm from the wall, keep the door seals clean and set the fridge to 3–5 °C. Longer runs than usual often mean a leaking seal or a dusty condenser.
tips.kettle: Boil only the water you need: a full kettle takes twice the time and energy of half a kettle.
tips.washer: Wash full loads in cold water; most of a washing machine's energy heats the water.
tips.tv: Lower the screen brightness and switch it off when nobody watches: standby still draws power.
tips.hifi: Amplifiers draw power even when idle; switch them off at the socket.
tips.dishwasher: Run only full loads on the eco programme, and skip heated drying when you can.
tips.microwave: For small portions a microwave uses less energy than the hob or the oven.
tips.toaster: High power in short bursts; unplug it when not in use.
tips.other: Energy not yet put down to a device. It shrinks as the system learns more of the home's devices.
